# Theme M1 — Local Setup GuideMixed multi-domain orchestrator (HR + Finance + Ops portals).  Produces aligned GT logs for UIA AutoSeg V2 evaluation.---## Prerequisites| Requirement | Notes ||---|---|| Python 3.11+ | Must be on PATH or at a standard install location || Google Chrome | Standard install at `C:\Program Files\Google\Chrome\` || ProcMine Desktop Agent | Must be running and recording before you start a session || ProcMine Browser Extension | Unpacked extension folder (one-time Chrome setup below) || Microsoft Excel | Optional — lookup steps are skipped if absent |> Teams, Outlook, and OneNote are **not required**. The orchestrator skips those noise steps automatically if the apps are not present.---## 1. Clone and install dependencies```powershellgit clone https://github.com/I-mBesideYou/procmine-test-sets.gitcd procmine-test-sets/Mixed/theme_m1_data/process_automationpip install pyautogui websocket-client```---## 2. One-time browser extension setupThe ProcMine browser extension captures browser navigation, clicks, and form inputs (L3 events). It must be loaded into each of the three Chrome portal windows once. After that it persists in the Chrome profiles stored at `theme_m1_data/chrome-profiles/` and loads automatically on every future run.**Step 1 — Get the extension**Download `procmine-extension-v1.0.0.zip` from the team drive and unzip it. Note the path to the unpacked folder (e.g. `C:\Users\<you>\Downloads\procmine-extension\`).**Step 2 — Run the one-time setup script**```powershellcd Mixed/theme_m1_data/process_automation$chrome = "C:\Program Files\Google\Chrome\Application\chrome.exe"$base   = "$PSScriptRoot\..\..\chrome-profiles"   # created automatically$ext    = "C:\Users\<you>\Downloads\procmine-extension"  # your path# Kill any existing Chrome, then open one window per portaltaskkill /F /IM chrome.exe 2>$null; Start-Sleep 2foreach ($entry in @(    @{dir="m1-hr";      url="http://127.0.0.1:5122/"},    @{dir="m1-finance"; url="http://127.0.0.1:5123/"},    @{dir="m1-ops";     url="http://127.0.0.1:5124/"})) {    New-Item -ItemType Directory -Force "$base\$($entry.dir)" | Out-Null    Start-Process $chrome -ArgumentList "--user-data-dir=`"$base\$($entry.dir)`"","--no-first-run","--new-window",$entry.url    Start-Sleep 3}```> The portals won't load (no http.server running yet) — that's fine. You just need Chrome open with each profile.**Step 3 — Load the extension in each window**In each of the 3 Chrome windows:1. Open a new tab → navigate to `chrome://extensions`2. Enable **Developer mode** (toggle, top-right)3. Click **Load unpacked** → select the `procmine-extension` folder4. Confirm extension ID `gfnbggcmaifligdcdiafmlbgpogheenn` appears5. Close the extensions tab**Step 4 — Close all Chrome windows**The extension is now saved to each profile. You're done — don't repeat this unless you delete `chrome-profiles/`.---## 3. One-time browser extension setupThe ProcMine browser extension captures browser navigation, clicks, and form inputs (L3 events). It must be loaded into each of the three Chrome portal windows once. After that it persists in the Chrome profiles stored at `theme_m1_data/chrome-profiles/` and loads automatically on every future run.**Step 1 — Get the extension**Download `procmine-extension-v1.0.0.zip` from the team drive and unzip it. Note the path to the unpacked folder (e.g. `C:\Users\<you>\Downloads\procmine-extension\`).**Step 2 — Run the one-time setup script**```powershellcd Mixed/theme_m1_data/process_automation$chrome = "C:\Program Files\Google\Chrome\Application\chrome.exe"$base   = "$PSScriptRoot\..\..\chrome-profiles"   # created automatically$ext    = "C:\Users\<you>\Downloads\procmine-extension"  # your path# Kill any existing Chrome, then open one window per portaltaskkill /F /IM chrome.exe 2>$null; Start-Sleep 2foreach ($entry in @(    @{dir="m1-hr";      url="http://127.0.0.1:5122/"},    @{dir="m1-finance"; url="http://127.0.0.1:5123/"},    @{dir="m1-ops";     url="http://127.0.0.1:5124/"})) {    New-Item -ItemType Directory -Force "$base\$($entry.dir)" | Out-Null    Start-Process $chrome -ArgumentList "--user-data-dir=`"$base\$($entry.dir)`"","--no-first-run","--new-window",$entry.url    Start-Sleep 3}```> The portals won't load (no http.server running yet) — that's fine. You just need Chrome open with each profile.**Step 3 — Load the extension in each window**In each of the 3 Chrome windows:1. Open a new tab → navigate to `chrome://extensions`2. Enable **Developer mode** (toggle, top-right)3. Click **Load unpacked** → select the `procmine-extension` folder4. Confirm extension ID `gfnbggcmaifligdcdiafmlbgpogheenn` appears5. Close the extensions tab**Step 4 — Close all Chrome windows**The extension is now saved to each profile. You're done — don't repeat this unless you delete `chrome-profiles/`.---## 3. Running a session**Start the ProcMine Desktop Agent first** and confirm it is recording.Then run either launcher:```powershell# PowerShell launcher (interactive prompts)cd Mixed/theme_m1_data/process_automation.\launch_m1.ps1# Or Python launcher (same behaviour, cross-platform args)python scripts/run_theme_m1.pypython scripts/run_theme_m1.py --seed 42 --speed 1 --scale 2```### Run parameters| Prompt / Flag | Values | Default ||---|---|---|| Seed | Any integer | Random || Speed | `1` = fast (0.4×) · `2` = normal (1.4×) | `2` || Scale | `1` = 5–7 procs · `2` = 8–10 · `3` = 11–14 | `2` || Date | `YYYY-MM-DD` | Today |Pre-set with env vars to skip prompts:```powershell$env:M1_SEED = "42"; $env:M1_SPEED = "1"; $env:M1_SCALE = "2".\launch_m1.ps1```### What launches- 3 Python `http.server` instances (ports 5122 / 5123 / 5124)- Notepad- Excel with `documents/m1_reference.xlsx` (if available)- 3 Chrome windows (HR / Finance / Ops portals), each with CDP and ProcMine extension### Extension checkThe launcher prints one of:```[OK] Extension loaded + NMH connected -> browser_* events WILL be captured``````[warn] Extension not found in profiles. Run one-time setup: ...```If you see the warn, do the one-time extension setup (section 2) before continuing.---## 4. OutputAfter the run, GT logs land in:```Mixed/theme_m1_data/gt-logs/  theme_m1_YYYYMMDD_HHMMSS.jsonl```Raw chunk arrives in S3 a few minutes after the session ends (desktop agent uploads asynchronously).---## 5. Per-chunk delivery packageOnce the chunk is in S3, generate the delivery package manually:```bashpython scripts/gen_chunk_package.py \  --gt    gt-logs/theme_m1_YYYYMMDD_HHMMSS.jsonl \  --out   gt-logs/theme_m1_YYYYMMDD_HHMMSS_package \  --events   /path/to/downloaded/events.jsonl \  --manifest /path/to/downloaded/manifest.json \  --s3-prefix s3://procmine-app/chunks/<uid>/<chunk_id>/```Then run the official self-check:```bashpython C:\Users\<you>\Downloads\uia_autoseg_chunk_report.py \  --events-jsonl /path/to/events.jsonl \  --manifest     /path/to/manifest.json \  --gt-jsonl     gt-logs/theme_m1_YYYYMMDD_HHMMSS.jsonl \  --no-run-pipeline --summary-only --pretty```Minimum pass criteria (from handoff doc section 4.4):```guardrails.status = pass (or warn)guardrails.failures = []manifest_event_line_count == actual event_count: OKGT/raw timestamp overlap: high (≥ 90%)```---## 6. # Theme M1 — Local Setup GuideMixed multi-domain orchestrator (HR + Finance + Ops portals).  Produces aligned GT logs for UIA AutoSeg V2 evaluation.---## Prerequisites| Requirement | Notes ||---|---|| Python 3.11+ | Must be on PATH or at a standard install location || Google Chrome | Standard install at `C:\Program Files\Google\Chrome\` || ProcMine Desktop Agent | Must be running and recording before you start a session || ProcMine Browser Extension | Unpacked extension folder (one-time Chrome setup below) || Microsoft Excel | Optional — lookup steps are skipped if absent |> Teams, Outlook, and OneNote are **not required**. The orchestrator skips those noise steps automatically if the apps are not present.---## 1. Clone and install dependencies```powershellgit clone https://github.com/I-mBesideYou/procmine-test-sets.gitcd procmine-test-sets/Mixed/theme_m1_data/process_automationpip install pyautogui websocket-client```---## 2. One-time browser extension setupThe ProcMine browser extension captures browser navigation, clicks, and form inputs (L3 events). It must be loaded into each of the three Chrome portal windows once. After that it persists in the Chrome profiles stored at `theme_m1_data/chrome-profiles/` and loads automatically on every future run.**Step 1 — Get the extension**Download `procmine-extension-v1.0.0.zip` from the team drive and unzip it. Note the path to the unpacked folder (e.g. `C:\Users\<you>\Downloads\procmine-extension\`).**Step 2 — Run the one-time setup script**```powershellcd Mixed/theme_m1_data/process_automation$chrome = "C:\Program Files\Google\Chrome\Application\chrome.exe"$base   = "$PSScriptRoot\..\..\chrome-profiles"   # created automatically$ext    = "C:\Users\<you>\Downloads\procmine-extension"  # your path# Kill any existing Chrome, then open one window per portaltaskkill /F /IM chrome.exe 2>$null; Start-Sleep 2foreach ($entry in @(    @{dir="m1-hr";      url="http://127.0.0.1:5122/"},    @{dir="m1-finance"; url="http://127.0.0.1:5123/"},    @{dir="m1-ops";     url="http://127.0.0.1:5124/"})) {    New-Item -ItemType Directory -Force "$base\$($entry.dir)" | Out-Null    Start-Process $chrome -ArgumentList "--user-data-dir=`"$base\$($entry.dir)`"","--no-first-run","--new-window",$entry.url    Start-Sleep 3}```> The portals won't load (no http.server running yet) — that's fine. You just need Chrome open with each profile.**Step 3 — Load the extension in each window**In each of the 3 Chrome windows:1. Open a new tab → navigate to `chrome://extensions`2. Enable **Developer mode** (toggle, top-right)3. Click **Load unpacked** → select the `procmine-extension` folder4. Confirm extension ID `gfnbggcmaifligdcdiafmlbgpogheenn` appears5. Close the extensions tab**Step 4 — Close all Chrome windows**The extension is now saved to each profile. You're done — don't repeat this unless you delete `chrome-profiles/`.---## 3. One-time browser extension setupThe ProcMine browser extension captures browser navigation, clicks, and form inputs (L3 events). It must be loaded into each of the three Chrome portal windows once. You just need Chrome open with each profile.**Step 3 — Load the extension in each window**In each of the 3 Chrome windows:1. Open a new tab → navigate to `chrome://extensions`2. Enable **Developer mode** (toggle, top-right)3. Click **Load unpacked** → select the `procmine-extension` folder4. Confirm extension ID `gfnbggcmaifligdcdiafmlbgpogheenn` appears5. Running a session**Start the ProcMine Desktop Agent first** and confirm it is recording.Then run either launcher:```powershell# PowerShell launcher (interactive prompts)cd Mixed/theme_m1_data/process_automation.\launch_m1.ps1# Or Python launcher (same behaviour, cross-platform args)python scripts/run_theme_m1.pypython scripts/run_theme_m1.py --seed 42 --speed 1 --scale 2```### Run parameters| Prompt / Flag | Values | Default ||---|---|---|| Seed | Any integer | Random || Speed | `1` = fast (0.4×) · `2` = normal (1.4×) | `2` || Scale | `1` = 5–7 procs · `2` = 8–10 · `3` = 11–14 | `2` || Date | `YYYY-MM-DD` | Today |Pre-set with env vars to skip prompts:```powershell$env:M1_SEED = "42"; $env:M1_SPEED = "1"; $env:M1_SCALE = "2".\launch_m1.ps1```### What launches- 3 Python `http.server` instances (ports 5122 / 5123 / 5124)- Notepad- Excel with `documents/m1_reference.xlsx` (if available)- 3 Chrome windows (HR / Finance / Ops portals), each with CDP and ProcMine extension### Extension checkThe launcher prints one of:```[OK] Extension loaded + NMH connected -> browser_* events WILL be captured``````[warn] Extension not found in profiles.
